_source: Official GATE 2027 DA syllabus (data/pyq/official_pdfs/DA/DA_GATE2027_syllabus.pdf), curated by hand: topics copied verbatim and split at the syllabus's own commas/semicolons; labelled groups kept whole.

_editorial.Section names: Each DA section has no sub-labels; the section is the subject. Machine Learning is split into its own labels Supervised / Unsupervised Learning.

Probability and Statistics: Sample space, events, independent events, mutually exclusive events
mean, median, mode and standard deviation
random variables, discrete random variables and probability mass functions
Continuous random variables and probability distribution function
uniform, exponential, Poisson, normal, standard normal, t-distribution, chi-squared distributions
confidence interval, z-test, t-test, chi-squared test

Linear Algebra: linear dependence and independence of vectors
matrices, projection matrix, orthogonal matrix, idempotent matrix, partition matrix and their properties
systems of linear equations and solutions; Gaussian elimination

Calculus and Optimization: Functions of a single variable, limit, continuity and differentiability

Programming, Data Structures and Algorit: basic data structures: stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, hash tables
Search algorithms: linear search and binary search
basic sorting algorithms: selection sort, bubble sort and insertion sort
basic graph algorithms: traversals and shortest path

Database Management and Warehousing: relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL
data types, data transformation such as normalization, discretization, sampling, compression
data warehouse modelling: schema for multidimensional data models, concept hierarchies, measures: categorization and computations

Supervised Learning: simple linear regression, multiple linear regression, ridge regression
cross-validation methods such as leave-one-out (LOO) cross-validation, k-folds cross-validation
Unsupervised Learning: hierarchical clustering, top-down, bottom-up: single-linkage, multiple-linkage

AI: reasoning under uncertainty topics — conditional independence representation, exact inference through variable elimination, and approximate inference through sampling
